Why is there an The American Electoral College?
Yes, no, no, no, maybe, yes, absolutely not, and no.

This is why

  • Trump won 2,626 Counties.
  • Hillary won 487 Counties.

The Electoral College is working as our founding fathers intended.

But Hillary won counties with significantly higher populations which is why, at least in my opinion, proportional representation in the senate is a better system for representing the minority since it works just as well if a minority's supporters are scattered throughout the country (thus to be unable to elect senators under the current system) or all in a single county. I kind of doubt that there are more religious conservatives than there are libertarians or leftist democrats but the system favors them because of having the regional concentration to be able to win states. I also want the ability to vote against the people in my state and have it count.

I find examples good ways to explain, so for example:

If county A has 100,000 people and they all want free food, and counties B-Q all produce food but only have a combined population of 70,000, the result will be county A is getting free food and counties B-Q all need to "just deal with it." They likely won't, and will stop producing food, meaning now all 170,000 people are screwed.

This is why letting the majority rule the minority is not a good idea; Rarely does the majority make good decisions for all involved, nor do they consider how it will impact people in a different geographic, economic, and/or cultural situation.

I'm not saying we should have absolute tyranny of majority, I'm just saying going by region isn't the best way to represent the minority these days since many minorities may not have a regional concentration (e.g. political party A is popular in regions B-Q with 1/3 of the overall vote, poltical party B is popular in region A with 1/3 of the overall vote, political party C is evenly distributed amongst all of the regions with 1/3 of the vote then the supporters of party C get no representation while party A gets favoritism) and therefore get no representation or perhaps someone wants more leverage to vote against people in their area (e.g. a Republican in California). Under the current system for how the senate is elected party A would have most of the seats while party B would have 2 seats and party C would have none. Under proportional representation Party A, B, and C would have about equal numbers of seats and perhaps parties A and C can form a coalition government. Also someone living in an area where 99% of the population supports party A can vote for party B or C and their vote will still mean something.
This is the point I'm trying to make about why we need proportional representation in congress as a better way to represent the minority

The founding fathers saw it as a way to protect the interests of minorities. Back in those days long-distance relocation wasn't nearly as common as it is today along with them not having the technologies we do today so culture in a specific area was much more set than it would be today. But in the age of the internet where I can live in the eastern US while listening to European music and watching Japanese porn and eating middle eastern food and using my Chinese smartphone all on a daily basis I think we start to see those regional barriers really start to break down. So it was a decent idea at the time when people would really need to assimilate with their local culture but in the modern world I think proportional representation in the senate would be a more effective way to represent minorities. There are still some minorities with enough regional concentration to win states and counties such as religious conservatives but other minorities whose supporters are scattered throughout the country such as libertarians and the more leftist Democrats (e.g. the Bernie Sanders crowd) will not have such luck. Proportional representation represents all minorities regardless of whether or not they have any regional concentration and allows your vote to count even if you want to vote against what 99% of the people in your area want (e.g. Republican in San Francisco).
